strategy.title: Singapore Space Sector: Next Bound of Development
strategy.owner: National Space Agency of Singapore (NSAS); the policy was announced in 2025 under the then Ministry of Trade and Industry and OSTIn
strategy.summary: Singapore's national space policy statement, announced 26 Feb 2025, sets out how Singapore will strengthen national space capabilities and create pathways to participate in the global space economy (NSAS Next Bound of Development page, last updated 25 Mar 2026). It is a government policy statement, not a statute. NSAS (from 1 Apr 2026) continues it. The 2 Feb 2026 speech adds the NSAS remit: national space capabilities including Earth observation, a multi-agency operations centre for satellite tasking and geospatial analytics, space situational awareness, equatorial and ASEAN partnerships, and space legislation and regulation.
strategy.budget: No strategy-level budget is stated. Programme funding quoted: the STDP page (updated 2 Jul 2026) says "As of 2025, OSTIn has secured $210m to advance technological innovation" (currency symbol as printed); the 2 Feb 2026 speech says the Government "has set aside over S$200 million since 2022" for space R&D through STDP. No NSAS operating budget was found.
goals: Strengthen Singapore's national capabilities in space (Next Bound of Development, 2025)
Create pathways for Singapore to participate in and contribute to the global space economy (Next Bound of Development, 2025)
Develop and operate national space capabilities, including Earth observation; set up a multi-agency operations centre for satellite tasking and geospatial analytics (2 Feb 2026 speech)
Build space situational awareness to protect space assets (2 Feb 2026 speech)
Deepen partnerships across the equatorial belt, ASEAN and emerging space nations (2 Feb 2026 speech)
Develop space legislation and regulation that is pro-innovation and addresses safety and sustainability (2 Feb 2026 speech)
strategy.law: No national space act in force. The 2 Feb 2026 speech says NSAS "will therefore also develop legislation and regulation for our space sector" and will engage the ecosystem on plans. No bill was found in opened sources. The 2024 Guidelines for Singapore-Related Space Activities are a guidance instrument, not a statute.

strategy.owner: Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth (submitter); approved by the Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (10 Dec 2024) and the government (December 2024).
strategy.summary: The Slovak government adopted the Slovak Space Strategy 2030+ in December 2024, after the Council for Science, Technology and Innovation approved it without comments on 10 December 2024 (resolution 2/31). The UN statement of June 2025 says it sets vision and goals for space activities, defines the competences of the responsible ministries, and records the current management system with a view to over-ministerial management. The strategy text itself was not read in this run because the slovak.space PDF did not load. Press reports (TASR, 18 Dec 2024) describe content areas: research and education, services for state administration and citizens, space industry, security and defence, and popularisation of space.

strategy.title: Slovenian Space Strategy 2030 (Small on Earth, big in space)
strategy.status: adopted by government decision 3 Nov 2023; identity of the adopted text not verified (attached PDF headed REVISED DRAFT)
strategy.owner: Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport at adoption (3 Nov 2023); now Ministry of Economy, Labour and Sport (GOV.SI)
strategy.summary: The government adopted Slovenia's first space strategy at a correspondence session on 3 November 2023, after an 18-month process run by the newly established Slovenian Space Office. It covers 2023 to 2030 with five pillars (technology and R&D, international cooperation, applications, STEM talent, entrepreneurship and spin-offs) and links the sector to ESA membership, EU programmes and the 2022 act. The PDF in the session folder is headed "REVISED DRAFT" in English and "REVIDIRAN OSNUTEK" in Slovene, so its text is cited as the draft.
strategy.budget: Approximately EUR 20 million in ESA contributions for 2023 to 2025 (strategy text, PDF p.11, draft). No overall national space budget line was found in the sources opened.
goals: Encourage and evolve space technologies and R&D, including satellite communication on Earth and beyond
Broaden participation in responsible international space exploration and research
Foster the development and uptake of space applications for a stronger commercial and sustainable future
Secure the future generation of scientists, engineers and young space professionals (STEM)
Stimulate entrepreneurship and university and RTO spin-offs through dedicated space innovation programmes
strategy.law: Space Activities Act (Zakon o vesoljskih dejavnostih, ZVDej), Uradni list RS 43/2022 (gazette dated 25 March 2022). Adopted by the National Assembly on 16 March 2022 and proclaimed by the President on 24 March 2022. Art. 4 assigns permits to the ministry responsible for technology; the ministry is not named in the act.

strategy.title: En strategi för svensk rymdverksamhet (Skr. 2017/18:259)
strategy.status: in force (still cited in the 2026 spring budget proposition; no successor strategy found)
strategy.horizon: Not specified in the proved text (long-term strategic goals)
strategy.owner: Government of Sweden, Ministry of Education (Utbildningsdepartementet); implemented by the Swedish National Space Agency (Rymdstyrelsen)
strategy.summary: Government communication of 9 May 2018 setting long-term strategic goals for Swedish space activity: freedom of action and access to space, a peaceful and sustainable use of space, the use of space data for society, international cooperation, industry and research, and legislation. A first defence and security strategy for space followed in July 2024. The 2026 spring budget proposition still refers to this strategy.
strategy.budget: 2026 spring amending budget (prop. 2025/26:99, 9 Apr 2026; government release 31 Mar 2026): SEK 400 million in higher appropriations to the Swedish National Space Agency and SSC Space AB, including SEK 14 million (agency, licensing) and SEK 386 million (capital injection to SSC Space AB in 2026). The same table reduces appropriation 3:4 Rymdforskning och rymdverksamhet by SEK 33.3 million. ESA subscription figure from the seed is NOT proved. Defence: SEK 1 billion for the Armed Forces, 2024-2032 (government decision, 4 Oct 2024).
goals: Ensure Swedish freedom of action in and access to space (säkerställa svensk handlingsfrihet i och tillgång till rymden), section 2.1
Prevent placing weapons in space and keep space from becoming an arena for conflict (förhindra utplacering av vapen i rymden)
Use space peacefully for human welfare and sustainable development, with transparency and openness
Secure data access for applications and services of societal benefit
Support industry, research and skills in space, and international and EU cooperation
Maintain legislation suited to space activities (see the new space law proposal)
strategy.law: Act on Space Activities (Lag 1982:963 om rymdverksamhet), issued 18 Nov 1982, amended up to SFS 2021:1025 (Riksdag register; ministry of record: Ministry of Justice). A new space law is in preparation: SOU 2021:91 "En ny rymdlag" (23 Nov 2021) proposed it; on 31 Mar 2026 the government called the 2026 licensing funding "a first and necessary step" toward it. No bill proved.

strategy.title: National Space Master Plan 2023-2037 (แผนแม่บทอวกาศแห่งชาติ พ.ศ. 2566-2580)
strategy.owner: National Space Policy Committee (NSPC) and Cabinet; implementation through GISTDA, MDES and ONDES
strategy.summary: The Cabinet approved the National Space Master Plan 2023-2037 on 13 Dec 2022 (Nation; Prachachat), with a draft National Communication Satellite Policy. The Cabinet said the plan would guide a space economy for national security, prosperity and sustainability. A 2023 public hearing on the draft plan and the draft Space Affairs Act described the plan as revisable every five years (Daily News, translation doubt on date). The NSPC approved draft space policies in July 2025 (Daily News). No Cabinet approval of a revised master plan and no Royal Gazette publication were found in the opened sources.
strategy.budget: No consolidated national space budget was found in the sources opened. Spending flows through agency budgets (GISTDA under MHESI; MDES). The annual budget bill and GISTDA budget documents were not opened, so this is an absence limited to the opened sources.
goals: Build a space economy for national security, prosperity and sustainability (Nation, 14 Dec 2022)
Use NASA expertise in space development (Nation, 14 Dec 2022)
Secure national communication satellite capacity, with NT assigned to advance the satellite policy within three years (Prachachat, 13 Dec 2022)
Open the satellite services market through a Landing Rights policy for foreign operators (draft, approved by NSPC 1/2568, Daily News 16 Jul 2025)
strategy.law: No space law in force. The draft Space Affairs Act was approved by the Cabinet on 13 Jul 2021 (Bangkok Post, 14 Jul 2021). It is not enacted in the sources opened. An 18 Aug 2026 report says the government is accelerating the Space Affairs Act (translation doubt on title).

strategy.title: Ensuring American Space Superiority (Executive Order 14369)
strategy.horizon: 2028 (crewed return to the Moon); 2030 (initial elements of a permanent lunar outpost)
strategy.owner: Executive Office of the President; the Assistant to the President for Science and Technology (APST) coordinates implementation (EO Sec. 3(a)).
strategy.summary: Executive Order 14369, dated 18 December 2025 and published in the Federal Register on 23 December 2025, sets national space priorities: returning Americans to the Moon by 2028 through Artemis, initial elements of a lunar outpost by 2030, and a space security strategy to be implemented by the APNSA with the Secretary of War within 180 days (Sec. 3(d)). It supersedes and revokes EO 14056 (National Space Council) and revises Space Policy Directive 3 on space traffic management (Sec. 4).
strategy.budget: The order sets no appropriation. The NASA FY2027 request is USD 18,829.1 million (NASA budget request summary, April 2026, 'NASA Total' row), against FY2026 at 24,438.3 million in the same row; column labels are not in the text extract. Congress passed continuing appropriations (P.L. 119-103, approved 2 Sept 2026) that expire 11 Dec 2026; the NASA rate under that Act was not stated in the sections read. The FY2027 Space Force request (about USD 71 billion, secondary press only) is not proved from an official budget document.
goals: Return Americans to the Moon by 2028 through the Artemis Program (Sec. 2(a)(i))
Establish initial elements of a permanent lunar outpost by 2030 (Sec. 2(a)(ii))
Implement a space security strategy within 180 days, led by the APNSA with the Secretary of War (Sec. 3(d))
Reform space acquisition at Commerce and NASA within 180 days (Sec. 3(c))
strategy.law: Executive order, not statute. EO 14369 is in the Federal Register (Vol. 90, No. 244, 23 Dec 2025, from the Dec 18, 2025 order). The statutes cited in the seed (National Aeronautics and Space Act 1958; Commercial Space Launch Act 1984) were not opened in this run and are not claimed here.

nodes.role: Lead ministry for civil space. The Minister, Prof. Blade Nzimande, is Executive Authority of SANSA under the SANSA Act and appointed the interim SANSA board (effective 21 Aug 2026).

nodes.name: South African National Space Agency (SANSA)
nodes.role: Civil space agency under the SANSA Act 36 of 2008; implementing agency for the National Space Programme; interim board from 21 Aug 2026 to Jan 2027.

nodes.role: Administers the Space Affairs Act (No. 84 of 1993) and is replacing it with a draft space industry regulatory bill. Minister Parks Tau.

nodes.name: South African Council for Space Affairs (SACSA)
nodes.role: Regulatory council under the Space Affairs Act. Dtic reply (5 Mar 2025): SACSA is 'the only competent regulatory body'; members were re-recruited from Aug 2024; one member reported appointed for 2026-2029 (secondary source).

nodes.name: South African Space Regulatory Council (SASREC) - proposed
nodes.role: Council proposed in the draft South African Space Industry Regulatory Bill; not established.

government.notes: Head of state and head of government: Cyril Ramaphosa is President (presidency homepage, fetched 27 Oct 2026); s.83 of the Constitution makes the President Head of State and head of the national executive. Lead body: DSTI (lead:true). The SANSA Act makes the Minister of Science, Technology and Innovation the Executive Authority; the Minister is named on SANSA's board notice (31 Aug 2026) and in the Parliament committee record of 29 Sep 2026. SANSA CEO Humbulani Mudau signed the 2025/26 Annual Report (31 Jul 2026). Space Affairs Act (1993) is administered by dtic; the SANSA Act (2008) governs SANSA. Local government elections were set for 4 Nov 2026 (SAnews, 30 Apr 2026); not used in this file.

strategy.title: National Space Strategy (NSS)
strategy.horizon: Not stated in the NSS text as read via SANSA's 2025 plan. SANSA Strategic Plan covers 2025/26-2029/30.
strategy.owner: Department of Science, Technology and Innovation (DSTI); implemented by SANSA. The 2008 National Space Policy (dtic) is the policy frame under the Space Affairs Act.
strategy.summary: The NSS sets three goals: a global share of the small-to-medium space systems market (knowledge economy and industrial competitiveness); better decision-making through integrating space and ground systems; and synergy and efficiency across the national space programme. SANSA's 2025-2030 plan treats the NSS and the SAEOS Strategy as directives that inform its work. Launch 2010 per Polity (10 Dec 2010); Cabinet approval date is given as 2008 by the same article.
strategy.budget: No NSS budget line. SANSA entity figures (SANSA plan 2025, Table 12): parliamentary grant R143.5m (2020, actual 143 464 R'000) to R137.6m (2025 revised, 137 643 R'000); R150.3m budgeted 2026; R160.3m 2027. Space Infrastructure Hub: R479.9m (2025 revised), R222.0m (2026 budget). The seed figure of about R350m is contradicted and rejected.
goals: Capture a global market share for small-to-medium space systems that supports a knowledge economy (NSS goal 1, SANSA plan 2025)
Empower better decision-making through the integration of space-based and ground-based systems (NSS goal 2)
Enhance synergy and efficiency across the national space programme (NSS goal 3)
Build human capital in space science and engineering (SANSA plan 2025, human capital outcomes)
Partner with spacefaring nations and extend space benefits across Africa (SANSA plan 2025 international cooperation)
strategy.law: Space Affairs Act No. 84 of 1993 (dtic) is cited as in operation in SANSA's 2025 plan. SANSA Act 36 of 2008 governs SANSA (board notice of 31 Aug 2026). A draft South African Space Industry Regulatory Bill would replace the 1993 Act and create SASREC; dtic told Parliament on 5 Mar 2025 that it 'will be processed and Gazetted during the 2025/2026 FY'. No gazetted bill or enacted replacement was found by 27 Oct 2026; status remains unconfirmed.

other_docs.title: SANSA Annual Report 2025/26
other_docs.note: Signed by CEO 31 Jul 2026 and Board Chair 31 Aug 2026 (PMG-hosted copy of the SANSA report). Records a clean audit and Board term ending 31 Aug 2026.

other_docs.title: Space Infrastructure Hub (SIH)
other_docs.note: DSTI national infrastructure programme supported by the Budget Facility for Infrastructure (PMG reply, 13 May 2025). Committee (29 Sep 2026) raised R296m underspending on SIH projects.

other_docs.note: Dtic-led draft replacing the Space Affairs Act; drafting since 2014; gazetting planned for FY2025/26 (PMG NW44, 5 Mar 2025). Status in 2026 unconfirmed.
